headline: A 5.8-billion-franc quarterly loss
text: On 4 February Credit Suisse reported a net loss of 5,828 million francs for the fourth quarter of 2015, including a goodwill write-off of 3,797 million, mostly in its trading business; the full-year 2015 loss was 2,944 million francs.
source: Credit Suisse Earnings Release 4Q15 (Form 6-K of 4 February 2016), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053092/000137036816000102/a160204g4q-ex99_1.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Credit Suisse branch in the Uraniastrasse, Zurich

headline: Banks roll over, commodities turn
text: On 17 February Glencore refinanced most of its $8.45bn revolving credit line early, with no financial covenants, and earlier in the month agreed a streaming deal on its Antapaccay copper mine in Peru. Commodities bounced off January lows: zinc averaged $1,710 a tonne, up 12%, iron ore rose 12% and oil steadied after falling near $30.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/early-refinancing-of-revolving-credit-facility/4295495; Investegate GLEN listing 11 Feb 2016 'Streaming Transaction - Antapaccay'; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Collahuasi copper mine, Chile, February 2016

headline: Oil sinks to $26
text: US crude fell to $26.19 a barrel on 11 February, the lowest since 2003 and a quarter of its 2014 level. Sanctions on Iran were lifted in January. The OPEC basket price was $22.48 on 20 January. US output has started to fall.

headline: ExxonMobil's profit halves
text: ExxonMobil reported on 2 February that it earned 16.15 billion dollars in 2015, half the 32.52 billion of 2014, and 2.78 billion in the fourth quarter, down 58 percent. It cut capital spending by 19 percent. US crude fell to about 26 dollars in mid-February, the lowest in more than a decade.
imageCaption: Exxon chief executive Rex Tillerson (left) with Vladimir Putin and Rosneft chief Igor Sechin, June 2012
imageCredit: Press Service of the President of Russia (kremlin.ru)

headline: Net debt falls to $25.9bn
text: Glencore's 2015 results on 1 March showed a net loss of $5.0bn after $5.8bn of write-downs and restructuring costs, but net debt down to $25.9bn from $30.5bn a year earlier. It aims for about $15bn by the end of 2017 and plans $4-5bn of asset sales in 2016. Oil recovered to an average $39 a barrel in March.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/preliminary-results-2015/4401444; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Collahuasi copper mine, Chile, February 2016

headline: Apple's first sales decline in years
text: On 26 April Apple reported revenue of 50.6 billion dollars for the quarter to March, down from 58 billion a year earlier, as iPhone sales fell; Tim Cook pointed to strong growth in services and more than a billion active Apple devices. Apple raised its capital return program to 250 billion dollars. In March 2015 Apple joined the Dow Jones index and in April 2015 its Watch went on sale.
imageCaption: The iPhone SE, introduced in March 2016

headline: Intel cuts 12,000 jobs and gives up on smartphones
text: Intel will cut 12,000 jobs, 11% of its workforce, by mid-2017 and make data centres and connected devices its main growth engines; Krzanich says Intel is evolving from a PC company into one that powers the cloud. It also cancelled its planned smartphone chips, effectively leaving that market.
source: https://www.cnbc.com/2016/04/19/intel-reports-q1-2016-earnings.html (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000050863/000005086316000122/pressreleaseq12016.htm (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich shows a chip at CES, January 2014

headline: 325,000 people reserve the Model 3
text: Tesla has unveiled the Model 3, its first car for the mass market, cheaper than its earlier models. Within a week more than 325,000 people paid to reserve one.
imageCaption: People queue outside the Tesla store in Frankfurt to reserve a Model 3 before it has even been shown, 31 March 2016

headline: Berkshire buys Apple shares
text: Berkshire disclosed that it began buying Apple shares in the first three months of the year, a rare investment in a technology company for a firm whose chairman has long avoided them.
imageCaption: Apple headquarters, Infinite Loop, Cupertino, California

headline: Pascal GPUs and growing demand for deep learning
text: On 6 May Nvidia unveiled its GeForce GTX 1080 and 1070 graphics cards on its new Pascal design. On 12 May it reported revenue of 1.30 billion dollars for the quarter, up 13%, with growth in games, professional graphics, data centres and cars; chief executive Jen-Hsun Huang said deep learning, a new computing model, is accelerating its growth.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581016000243/q117pr.htm (Nvidia press release of 12 May 2016, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jensen Huang presents Nvidia's Pascal GPUs at Computex, Taipei, 31 May 2016

headline: Britain votes to leave the EU
text: In the referendum of 23 June, 51.9 percent of British voters chose to leave the European Union on a turnout of 72 percent. Prime Minister David Cameron announced his resignation. The pound fell to a 31-year low against the dollar and stock markets fell around the world on the day after the vote.
imageCaption: David Cameron, with his wife Samantha, announces his resignation outside 10 Downing Street the morning after the referendum, 24 June 2016

headline: The Gotthard Base Tunnel opens
text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel was inaugurated on 1 June. At 57 kilometres it is the longest railway tunnel in the world, the first flat, low-level route through the Alps, for trains between central Switzerland and Ticino. Regular service begins in December.
imageCaption: Celebrations for the opening of the Gotthard Base Tunnel, June 2016

headline: Ten-year yields at a record low after the Brexit vote
text: After Britain voted on 23 June to leave the European Union, investors bought safe government bonds. The 10-year Treasury yield averaged 1.5 percent in July, the lowest monthly average on record. US inflation is about 1 percent (June), and the Fed has kept its rate at 0.25 to 0.5 percent since December. Gold averaged 1,337 dollars, 5 percent more than in June.
imageCaption: David Cameron announces his resignation outside 10 Downing Street after the Brexit vote, 24 June 2016

headline: Wal-Mart buys Jet.com to fight Amazon
text: On 8 August Wal-Mart agreed to buy the online retailer Jet.com for 3.3 billion dollars. Jet's founder Marc Lore will lead Wal-Mart's US online business, which is growing far more slowly than Amazon.

headline: OPEC and Russia agree to cut
text: At its 30 November conference OPEC agreed to cut about 1 million barrels a day for the first half of 2017, its first cut since 2008, with Russia and other non-members promising further reductions. Oil prices jumped and US crude ended the month near $49.

headline: Trump wins the presidency
text: Donald Trump, a businessman who has never held office, won the US presidential election of 8 November against Hillary Clinton, carrying Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, while Clinton leads in the national vote. He promises tax cuts, less regulation, infrastructure spending and tariffs. After falling overnight, US shares rose to records, led by banks: the KBW bank index gained more than 17 percent in November.
imageCaption: Donald Trump speaks after Hillary Clinton's concession, New York, 9 November 2016

headline: Record revenue, up 54%
text: On 10 November Nvidia reported record revenue of 2.00 billion dollars for the quarter to October, 54% more than a year earlier, and record profit margins, with demand from data centres for AI growing.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang at Nvidia's GTC Taiwan, September 2016

headline: James Quincey to succeed Muhtar Kent as chief executive
text: On 9 December Coca-Cola announced that president and chief operating officer James Quincey, a 20-year company veteran, will succeed Muhtar Kent as chief executive on 1 May 2017; Kent stays chairman. Coca-Cola is in the middle of refranchising its North American bottling territories to independent bottlers, which shrinks its revenue but raises its margins.

headline: Boeing signs a 16.6 billion dollar deal with Iran Air
text: On 11 December Boeing and Iran Air signed an agreement for 80 aircraft, 50 737s and 30 777s, valued at 16.6 billion dollars at list prices, the first such deal between an American company and Iran since 1979. Deliveries are planned over ten years from 2018. Washington licensed the sales in September under the nuclear deal.
imageCaption: An Iran Air aircraft at Tehran's Imam Khomeini airport, 2016
